cd ~/Library/Application\ Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/projects/p-3481b66bf01d02f-fa8baffc9e83e956 && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json
d=json.load(open('current-state.json'))['state']
conv=d['conversations'][0]
print("=== MESSAGES", len(conv['messages']))
for m in conv['messages']:
    keys=[k for k in m if k not in ('text','content','fileReport')]
    print("\n--- id=%s role=%s kind=%s at=%s" % (m.get('id'), m.get('role'), m.get('kind'), m.get('createdAt')))
    for k in sorted(m.keys()):
        v=m[k]
        if k in ('text','content'):
            print(f"  {k}:\n" + "\n".join("    | "+l for l in str(v).splitlines()))
        elif k=='fileReport':
            print(f"  fileReport: {str(v)[:300]}...")
        else:
            s=json.dumps(v); print(f"  {k}: {s[:200]}")
print("\n=== TOOL ACTIVITIES", len(d['toolActivities']))
for t in d['toolActivities']:
    print(f"\n{t['actionId']} seq={t['seq']} corr={t.get('correlationId')} {t['tool']} [{t['actionClass']}] state={t['state']} title={t.get('title')}")
    print("   args:", t['arguments'][:300])
    print("   result:", (t.get('result') or '')[:300])
print("\n=== CHANGES")
for c in d['changes']: print(c)
print("\n=== printIntent", conv.get('printIntent'), "setupIntent", conv.get('setupIntent'))
print("resumeCheckpoint summary:", json.dumps(conv.get('resumeCheckpoint'))[:1500])
EOF

#### writing UI code section
## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). Change the
   token file to match, or, when the code's value is the one to keep, change
   the artifact first. Do not trust old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
     translucent rounded rectangles.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:

# Figma mirror: tools and backups

> **2026-10-20: Figma is retired and out of date.** The two Claude artifacts are now the up-to-date JusPrin
> design. Do NOT re-sync them from Figma: that would overwrite newer design work. Edit them directly:
> copy the live files into `work/` (or read them with the Artifact tool), change them, publish only the changed
> files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. Remember the canvas keeps its own copy of the design system in
> `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens and component styles): change both artifacts together. `tools/composer/` holds
> the scripts used since then (`render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome; `resize_board.py` fixes a
> board's height in its file and in `canvas.json`). The Figma re-sync steps below are kept as history.


This folder keeps what is needed to re-sync two Claude artifacts with the Figma file "JusPrin v2"
(file key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`), and to prove a re-sync breaks nothing.

- Canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
- JusPrin Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL

It lives outside the JusPrin repo on purpose: it is not product code, and untracked files in the repo mean
"unfinished work" there.

## What is here

- `published/` — an exact copy of what is published now (`canvas/project`, `ds/project`). Every re-sync is
  compared against it, then it is replaced by the new build.
- `figma/spec3/<page id>.txt` — the Figma pages as last read (one text line per layer). `figma/vars.json` —
  Figma's variables, text styles and shadows as last read.
- `tools/` — the scripts (below).
- `visual/figma/*.png` — Figma's own screenshot of each page, used to score the artboards.
  `visual/scores-*.json` — the scores before and after the 2026-10-13 re-import.
- `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` — the published files, the Figma reads and the scripts as they were
  before the re-import of 2026-10-13. Running those scripts on those reads reproduces those files byte for byte.

## Re-sync, step by step

1. Read Figma. For each page id (`0:1 1423:396 320:1053 160:59 9:153 359:116 1148:1287 1258:396 1328:2780`)
   call the Figma tool `use_figma` with the text of `tools/spec3_min.js`, replacing `__PAGE__` and `__OFFSET__`
   (0, then 20200, 40400, ... while the offset is below the returned `total`). About 35 calls; have background
   agents make them, because each reply is large. Run `tools/vars.js` once the same way and save its result as
   `figma/vars.json`. The script source is `tools/figma_spec3.js`; `python3 tools/minify.py tools/figma_spec3.js
   tools/spec3_min.js` rebuilds the one-line version.
2. Decode the replies from the session transcripts:
   `SESSION=<session id> OUT=figma python3 tools/collect.py`
3. Build into a scratch folder `new/`:

       export FIGMA_DIR=$PWD/figma DS_DIR=$PWD/new/ds REPO=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin
       rm -rf new && mkdir new && cp -R published/ds new/ds
       python3 tools/build_variants.py $REPO new/ds
       python3 tools/build_canvas.py $REPO new/canvas <design system version id>
       mkdir -p new/specs/project/screens && cp published/ds/project/tokens.json new/specs/project/
       python3 tools/specs.py $REPO figma/spec3 new/specs/project/screens

4. Compare with what is published: `python3 tools/compare_builds.py published new`. With no change in Figma and
   no change in the scripts, every line must say "identical". Explain every file that is not before publishing.
5. Compare with Figma itself: take a screenshot of each Figma page (`get_screenshot`, maxDimension 8000) into
   `visual/figma/`, then `tools/visual_pages.py`, screenshot each `composite-<page>.html` at full page size,
   and `tools/visual_compare.py`. No artboard may score worse than in `visual/scores-after.json`.
6. Publish only the changed files to the same artifact URLs, check the live pages, then replace `published/`.

"""Makes room for the taller Composer: the content area just above the Composer frame shrinks and clips instead of
running under the box or pushing it out of the pane. Usage: fit_content.py <canvas project dir> <board>..."""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path
from htmlfrag import element_at, TAG
proj = Path(sys.argv[1])
for name in sys.argv[2:]:
    f = proj / name; s = f.read_text()
    i = s.index('data-n="Composer box"')
    stack = []
    for m in TAG.finditer(s):
        if m.start() >= i: break
        close, tag, selfclose = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        if tag in ('path', 'circle', 'rect', 'line', 'polyline', 'polygon', 'img') or selfclose: continue
        if close: stack.pop()
        else: stack.append(m.start())
    frame, pane = stack[-2], stack[-3]  # stack[-1] is the Composer box itself
    # the frame's previous sibling inside the pane
    j = s.index('>', pane) + 1; prev = None
    while j < frame:
        a, b = element_at(s, j); prev = a; j = b
    end = s.index('>', prev)
    tag = s[prev:end]
    m = re.search(r'style="([^"]*)"', tag); st = m.group(1)
    add = ''
    if 'flex:1 1 0' not in st: add += 'flex:1 1 0;'
    if 'min-height:0' not in st: add += 'min-height:0;'
    if 'overflow:hidden' not in st: st2 = st + ';overflow:hidden'
    else: st2 = st
    st2 = st2.replace('box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;', 'box-sizing:border-box;flex:none;' + add, 1) if add else st2
    s = s[:prev] + tag.replace(m.group(0), f'style="{st2}"', 1) + s[end:]
    f.write_text(s); print(name, 'added', add or '-', 'overflow')

---
name: agent-turn-activity-proposal
description: "2026-10-20: one 'yes' drew 17 tool cards + 17 empty bubbles + 8 change rows; proposal board on the JusPrin v2 canvas (Agent UI page, x 9209) replaces per-call cards with one Chat/System Line per turn; rules, board builder, Kenneth's decision pending."

  type: project
---

On 2026-10-20 Kenneth looked at a live chat ("Affirmative Response Without Context", project arrow_headband)
where he answered "yes" to switching to the Bambu Lab A1 and the thread grew by 17 Chat/Tool Activity
cards (12 read-only lookups, 5 edits), 17 empty assistant bubbles (one per model response that only called
tools), 8 change rows, then the reply: about three screens for one word. He asked for a new UX.

What I found before proposing:
- The approved print-timeline board on the canvas draws an Agent turn as prose + one summary line
  ("Laid flat · 5 walls · 35% gyroid · +3⌄"); no per-call cards anywhere in the design. The Chat/System
  Line component is specified as "quiet one-line record of ... background agent work".
- The Tool Activity card was designed for approvals (Pending / Approve / Reject); approvals were removed
  2026-10-07 ([[tool-call-approval-removed]]), so the card has no question left to ask.
- Structural cause of the splitting: MessageList groups activities under the assistant message that
  carries their correlationId, and every tool-only response is its own empty message, so one turn becomes
  17 groups and the change rows cannot merge (groupChanges only merges within a block). All 17 messages
  carry inReplyTo m-3, so grouping by turn needs no saved-data change.

The proposal (board "agent-turn-activity · proposal", page Agent UI, x 9209 y 3030, 986×3213; builder
`figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_turn_activity_board.py` reading `turn_yes.json` pulled from the saved
chat): (1) while working, one Chat/System Line under the person's message with the running action's
title + Stop; (2) finished, the same line reads "{n} actions ⌄", the reply lands under it, the turn's
changes follow as one merged block (printer_setup = one row with process and filament in the meta;
3 placements = "3 steps merged"); (3) opened, one line per action, edits in text/primary, lookups in
text/secondary, failures in status/danger with the message. Measured work (slice) keeps its progress card.

**How to apply:** every string on a proposal board must come from the saved chat or a named rule
([[mockup-strings-from-real-output]]). Kenneth has not decided yet; check the chat before implementing.

are not chips because the model did not end with "Choices: a | b"; printer_setup_preview said Textured
Cool Plate but printer_setup applied Smooth High Temp Plate.

content.text:
Done. The picture is attached above, and the same board is now on the JusPrin v2 canvas as "agent-turn-activity · proposal" on the Agent UI page, to the right of the two earlier proposals: https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v

**What your "yes" produced.** The model answered with 17 tool calls before it said a word. Twelve were lookups (listing presets, previewing the setup, analysing fit, picturing the plate, inspecting the workspace) and five changed the project (the printer switch, three placements, one arrange). The app draws every call as a raised "Done" card, and because each tool-only response is its own assistant message, each card also sits under an invisible empty bubble and gets its own change rows. The thread grew by 42 items, about three screens, and then the reply listed the same changes a third time under "What changed".

**Why it looks like this.** The Tool Activity card was designed for the approval flow, where each card asked Approve or Reject. Approvals were removed on 2026-10-07, so the card no longer has a question to ask, but it is still drawn for every call. The approved print-timeline board on the canvas never draws per-call cards: an agent turn there is prose plus one summary line, and the design system defines Chat/System Line as the "quiet one-line record of background agent work".

**The proposal** applies those two design decisions to this real turn. Every string on the board is from the saved chat or produced by a rule the captions name.

1. **While the agent works:** one line under your message with the running action's title and a Stop link, instead of cards appearing one by one. Work with measured progress, like slicing, keeps its progress card.
2. **Finished:** the line stays put and reads "17 actions ⌄"; the reply lands under it; the turn's changes follow as one block. Rows merge per turn, so the printer switch is one row with its process and filament in the meta, and the three placements are one "3 steps merged" row with Revert.
3. **Opened:** one line per action, in order. Edits read in text/primary, lookups in text/secondary, a failed action in status/danger with its message.

Saved data does not change: all 17 messages already record that they reply to your "yes", so the grouping is a rendering change in MessageList.tsx, plus one host change so a printer setup records one change instead of three preset switches.

**Three things I noticed on the way, not part of the proposal:**
- The chat title "Affirmative Response Without Context" came from a title generator that was given only the word "yes".
- The reply's three numbered options did not become tap chips because the model ended with "Which would you like?" instead of the "Choices: a | b | c" line the page looks for.
- The setup preview promised Textured Cool Plate, but applying the setup produced Smooth High Temp Plate. The preview and the apply disagree.

**Your decisions**, each in full:

- Should the line's collapsed text be the plain count "17 actions", or should it also say what changed, for example "17 actions · 3 changes"? The count alone is what I drew, because the change rows underneath already say what changed and a second count invites confusion. Adding the changes count makes the line more informative when the rows are far below. I recommend the count alone.
- Should the opened log hide the lookups entirely and show only the five edits? Hiding them makes the log short and readable, but it loses the audit of what the agent looked at, which is what you want when it does something odd. I recommend showing all actions with the two text colours, as drawn.

content.text:
All three points are in the revised board, which is republished on the canvas and attached above together with the two reference screenshots.

**1. Restore points during a turn.** Yes, the mid-turn Revert buttons are real, and stopping them is a small change. Versions are not saved per change. The autosave probe in ProjectAutosave.cpp runs every 2 seconds and captures a version whenever the model changed and 1.5 seconds have passed quietly. The agent's edits in this turn came 3 to 9 seconds apart, so each one became a version, five in total. The fix is a "turn in flight" predicate on the autosave, wired from ShellController.cpp where it already wires the agent host's turn-boundary callback, so the probe skips the capture while the agent is busy, and one capture runs at the turn boundary. That boundary already fires both when the reply finishes and when you press Stop, so a stopped turn still gets its version. The board now shows one Revert per turn, on its last row.

**2. Stop.** Agreed, and the composer's Stop already does this. It sends the host a stop request, the host cancels the model stream, marks the message Stopped and fires the turn boundary. One limit worth knowing: a native tool that is already running, say an arrange, finishes on its own. Only the model stops asking for more. The Stop link on the line is gone from the board.

**3. How ChatGPT and Claude draw it.** I looked at both in your Chrome rather than relying on memory. ChatGPT draws one grey line above the reply, "Worked for 1m 9s >", with a hairline under it. Opened, it shows the agent's interim narration and summary rows such as "Used the browser, ran commands". Claude draws "Read memory, searched past chats, searched the web >" in the same place. Opened, it is a bordered list with one row per tool, the tool name followed by its argument, plus short italic lines of reasoning between them. Both apps shimmer the words while working. I did not run a live turn in either account, so the ticking-seconds animation during a turn is from memory, not verified. Each closes the activity into one line when the turn ends, which is what the board proposes.

The board now reads "Preview a printer setup… · 6s" while working, with the seconds counting up and the words shimmering, and "Worked for 44s · 17 actions ⌄" when finished. Both numbers come from timestamps in the saved chat.

One design-system note. The shimmer is motion, and the design system has no motion token yet. Adding it means one duration token in the Design System artifact and the guard test, before any code types a number.

**Your decision:**

- Should the opened list stay one plain line per action, as drawn, or follow Claude's style of a bordered list with the tool name separated from its argument, for example "Place" followed by "arrow headband.STL: move to 128, 128"? The plain lines reuse Chat/System Line with nothing new. The split style reads better but needs the host to send the title in two parts, which is a protocol addition. I recommend the plain lines first and the split later if the log gets used.
plain lines first. go ahead and implement it

description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

Implemented, built, and tested. The changes are uncommitted on jusprin-newui, and the rebuilt app is running now at the Home screen with the arrow headband project ready to open.

**What changed for the person.** In the project chat a turn is now one item: your message, one quiet line for the Agent's work, its reply, then the turn's changes as one block. While the turn runs the line reads the action in flight and the seconds since your message, ticking and shimmering, for example "Preview a printer setup… · 6s". When it ends the line reads "Worked for 44s · 17 actions" and opens into one plain line per action, edits in the primary text colour, lookups in secondary, a failed one in red with its message. Empty tool-only bubbles are gone. A printer setup's three preset switches read as one row, "Switched to Bambu Lab A1" with the process and filament in the meta, and three placements merge into one "3 steps merged" row. The printer panel is untouched.

**The mid-turn restore points had a different cause than I first said.** They did not come from the autosave probe. Before every mutating tool call the shell pinned a version, and after it saved again, so each agent edit cost two full project saves. Now the first edit of a model turn pins once, later edits in the same turn reuse that version, the turn's end saves the result through the existing chat checkpoint, and the autosave probe holds its model capture while a turn runs. Stop still works through the composer and still ends the turn with that one save. An edit from an external MCP client outside a turn behaves as before.

**Verified:**
- Page tests: 553 pass, including new tests for the turn line, the opened log, the ticking clock, the merged rows, and the printer panel staying as it was.
- Agent bridge tests: 381 pass, with a new check that messages reach the page stamped with their time.
- Token guard passes with the one new motion token.
- The production thread components render the saved "yes" chat as shown in the picture above.

**Not verified, and why.** The app's web view ignores background clicks, so I could not open the project in the running app from here. Two things need a real model turn, which the spend rule says I should not run without your go-ahead: the shimmering, ticking line during a turn, and that only one Revert appears per turn afterwards. Opening the arrow headband project in the app that is running now and sending any request that edits the plate would show both.

content.text:
Both changed, rebuilt, and the app is relaunched with the new page so you can see them live.

**The chevron.** You were half right, and the convention depends on where the chevron sits. A chevron at the far edge of a row points down when closed and up when open, which is what Bootstrap and GitHub's Primer do and what I had drawn. A chevron right after the words points right when closed and down when open, which is what ChatGPT, Claude and Apple's disclosure controls do. Since you read it the second way, the line now puts the chevron right after the words, pointing right while closed and down once open, as in the picture above.

**The running glyph.** Agreed, a still arrow says nothing. The glyph now rotates once a second while the turn runs, both on the line and on a running action inside the opened log, and it stops when the turn ends. The words next to it keep their shimmer. Readers who asked their system for reduced motion get a still glyph and plain words. The one-second period is a new token next to the shimmer one, guarded by the token test.

Verified: the page suite passes at 555 tests with two new ones for the glyph states, the token guard passes, and the rebuilt bundle inside the app carries the spinner. The rotation itself cannot show in a still picture, so that part is for you to see in the running app, which is open at Home with the arrow headband project ready.

Sources on the convention: [Primer, progressive disclosure](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/progressive-disclosure), [an ESRF discussion comparing MUI, Ant Design, Bootstrap and Headless UI](https://gitlab.esrf.fr/icat/data-portal/-/merge_requests/415), [Michael Tsai on the iOS and Android chevrons](https://mjtsai.com/blog/?p=31439).

# ChatToolActivity

The card under an Agent message that shows one action the Agent wants to take or is taking, from asking permission to the outcome.

- You supply `title` (what the action is: "Update print settings"), `status`, and `message` (one line for that status). For `pending` pass `onApprove` and `onReject`; for `running` pass `progress` (0 to 100, or leave it out when unknown) and `onCancel`.
- Statuses: `pending` waits for approval with Approve and Reject; `running` shows a `Progress` track and a Cancel link; `succeeded` and `failed` report the result; `cancelled` and `rejected` say that nothing changed.
- A `surface-subtle` card with a 1px `border-subtle` stroke, `radius-medium` corners and `space-12` padding, 300px wide. The title is `body-small-bold`; every status line is a 16px glyph plus `body-small` text, so status never rests on colour alone. Success uses `status-success` and failure `status-danger`.
- Write the message so it stands alone: "Applying changes · 60%", "Couldn't save changes. Please try again.", "Rejected. Your settings are unchanged."
- One card per action. A connection that needs a code composes a `FieldSecret` beside it rather than adding a variant.

</artifact-file-content>

<artifact-file-content>
JusPrin makes advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. It is a dense, native desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a chat Agent beside the 3D workspace. Build every surface to feel focused, assured, inventive and approachable.

## Voice and name

- Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Set it in the surrounding text colour; never put the gradient on small text.
- Be direct, capable and optimistic. Never cute, cryptic or over-engineered.
- Prefer plain language to slicer jargon. Say "Slice plate", not "Generate G-code".
- Make the next action obvious. One `ButtonPrimary` per view names the thing the screen is for; everything else is quieter.
- Buttons and labels are sentence case, verb first, with no full stop: "Add printer", "Open printer settings", "Undo".
- Address the person as "you". The Agent speaks as "I". No emoji anywhere in the product.
- A status is never colour alone: pair the colour with an icon and a plain-language label, such as a `circle-alert` glyph beside "Printer offline".

## Logo

- Use the files in `assets/Logos` as they are. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, recolour, outline, shadow or take the mark apart.
- Default to `jusprin-mark.svg` for application icons and small product contexts, and to the horizontal lockup when there is room for the name.
- Place the logo only on `neutral-white`, `neutral-mist`, `neutral-ink` or another quiet solid field, never over an image or pattern.
- Keep clear space of at least a quarter of the mark's width on every side.
- Minimum sizes on screen: 24px for the mark, 120px wide for the horizontal lockup. Below that, use the mark alone.
- Use the single-ink marks only when the gradient cannot be shown: `jusprin-mark-ink.svg` on light grounds, `jusprin-mark-white.svg` on dark ones.

## Colour

- Style product UI with the semantic tokens (`surface-*`, `text-*`, `border-*`, `action-*`, `status-*`). The primitives (`brand-*`, `neutral-*`) are the palette behind them, for brand artwork and covers, not a component API. The one exception is `Tooltip`, which is `neutral-ink` with `neutral-white` text in both modes.
- Page background is `surface-canvas`. Sidebars and grouped settings sit on `surface-subtle`. Dialogs, menus and popovers sit on `surface-raised` with an elevation shadow. A highlighted row inside them (hover or keyboard focus) is filled with `surface-raised-hover`, not `surface-subtle`, which would look sunk in on a dark menu.
- Body copy and values are `text-primary`; descriptions are `text-secondary`; metadata and placeholders are `text-tertiary`.
- `action-primary` is for the decisive action, the selected segment and text links. It is Orbit purple in light mode and Bloom pink in dark mode, so always put `action-on-primary` on it, never a literal white.
- Dark mode is a remapping of the same token names, not an inversion. Keep hierarchy, density and geometry identical and let the tokens change the values.
- The signature gradient runs from `brand-orbit` to `brand-bloom`. Reserve it for the logo, the splash screen, onboarding and rare hero moments. Never use it as ordinary product chrome.
- `axis-x`, `axis-y` and `axis-z` belong to the 3D viewport only. Never use them for status.
- A failed print or task is reported on `surface-failure-inverse`, a dark panel in both modes, with the `text-on-failure-*`, `status-danger-on-inverse` and `border-on-failure` tokens. Do not mix the ordinary text tokens onto it.

## Typography

- One family for all product UI: HarmonyOS Sans SC in Regular (400) and Bold (700), with the system UI font as fallback. There are no other weights and no italics.
- Use the ten type styles as they are and pick the nearest one; never set a bespoke size. `page-title` 24/30, `section` 18/24, `body` 14/20, `body-small` 13/18, `label` 12/16, `metadata` 10/14, each with a bold partner.
- Bold is for emphasis inside a run of the same size: the primary action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside its detail.
- `code` (12/16, the system monospace font) is only for code, keys, file paths, commands and IDs. Names, words, numbers and measurements stay in the sans face; its digits are already equal width, so changing values do not shift.
- Letter spacing is 0 everywhere. Capitals are reserved for short eyebrow captions set in `metadata-bold`, such as "CURRENT SETUP", "STEP 1 OF 3" and menu section titles; type them in capitals rather than transforming the text.

## Layout and geometry

- Whole-screen structure (top bar, panes, where menus open) is in the Application layout section. Every screen in the design file is on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), one page per page of the design file, and is specified layer by layer in the files under `screens/`.
- Design for a dense desktop application measured in device-independent pixels. Do not import web habits: no oversized controls, blur, glass or hero spacing inside the application shell.
- Space with the scale only: `space-4`, `space-8`, `space-12`, `space-16`, `space-20`, `space-24`, `space-32`, `space-40`, `space-48`.
- Controls take `radius-small` (4px). Containers such as cards, popovers and chat bubbles take `radius-medium` (8px), and so does `ButtonPrimary`, the one branded action. Sheets and large dialogs take `radius-large` (12px). Radii of 16px and above are for onboarding and marketing only.
- Borders are 1px `border-subtle`, drawn inside the box so a bordered control keeps its stated height.
- Control heights are compact: 26px for fields, selects and text links, 28px for chips and reply choices, 30px for a segmented control, 32px for a secondary or icon button, 34px for a primary or split button, 36px for a menu row.
- Shadows mark elevation, not decoration: `elevation-subtle` for tooltips, `elevation-medium` for menus and popovers, `elevation-strong` for sheets and dialogs. Flat surfaces carry no shadow.
- Every progress track is `component-progress-height` (4px) thick.

## Iconography

- Functional icons are Lucide 1.47.0 outlines, kept unchanged in `assets/Icons`. Inline the SVG and colour it with the surrounding text token through `currentColor`.
- Draw icons at 16, 20 or 24px. The only exception is the 14px fact glyph inside the setup card (`component-setupCard-iconSize`).
- Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom; do not approximate them with Lucide glyphs, and do not decorate with logo-derived shapes where a functional icon is clearer.
- No emoji and no filled icon sets.

## Components and states

- Every interactive component defines normal, hover, pressed, disabled and keyboard-focus states, plus success, warning and error where they apply.
- Hover and pressed change the fill, not the size: quiet controls go to `surface-subtle` then `surface-selected`; the primary action goes to `action-primary-hover` then `action-primary-pressed`.
- Fields show state on their stroke: 1px `border-subtle` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, 2px `border-focus` when focused, 1px `status-danger` with a message when wrong, and an `action-disabled` fill when disabled.
- Disabled controls keep their shape. Filled and icon buttons drop to 40% opacity, outlined buttons to 50%; fields, selects and chips switch to `action-disabled` and `action-disabled-text`. Do not hide a disabled action.
- Actions: `ButtonPrimary` once per view, `ButtonSecondary` for other labelled actions, `ButtonIcon` when a glyph alone is unmistakable, `ButtonLink` for low-emphasis moves such as "‹ Back" and "Undo", and `ButtonSplit` when the main action has alternatives.
- Entry: `FieldText`, `FieldSecret` for codes and keys, `FieldSearch` to filter a list, `FieldNumber` for one parameter, `FieldVerificationCode` for a six-digit code. Choice: `SegmentedControl` for two to five short options, `Select` for more, `Checkbox` for on or off, `Swatch` for a filament colour.
- Menus are a `MenuPopover` of `MenuRow`s, grouped with `MenuSectionTitle`. Focused tasks sit in a `Sheet`; an action that cannot be undone asks first with `DialogConfirmation`.
- Canvas tools use a `ToolPanel` of `FormRow`s. Status is shown with `StatusDot` and `Progress`, always beside words. `Stepper` marks position in a short setup sequence; `Tooltip` names icon-only controls; `DisclosureTechnicalDetails` folds away secondary detail.
- The Agent pane is built from `ChatHeader`, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatReplyChoice`, `ChatAttachment`, `ChatToolActivity` and `Composer`. The header carries `ChipPrinterSpool`; the Home screen lists `ProjectCard`s and `PrinterCard`s.
- Draw every glyph with `Icon`.

## Accessibility

- Text meets 4.5:1 on the surface its token names; large text, control boundaries that carry meaning, icons and focus rings meet 3:1.
- Keyboard focus is a visible 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px. Never signal focus with a fill change alone.
- `status-warning` is the one exception in light mode, at about 2.5:1 on `surface-canvas`: use it for the warning glyph only, beside a `text-primary` label.
- `border-subtle` is decorative. A control must be recognisable by its label or glyph without it.

## Not synced

This design system and the JusPrin v2 canvas are the up-to-date JusPrin design. They began on 2026-10-13 as copies of a Figma file; since 2026-10-20 Figma is retired and out of date, and changes are made here directly. The font files cover Latin only; Chinese, Korean and Thai text falls back to the system font. `code` is the system monospace stack the application ships. Each component card shows its variants in light and in dark; where no dark variant is drawn, the dark panel is the light variant with the Dark values of the same tokens. Photographs and 3D renders appear as flat placeholders, and artwork larger than 64px is not drawn. The Agent cards and the components on the review page are on the canvas and in `screens/` but are not built as coded components.

content.text:
Both fixed and published.

**The centred text.** WebKit centres the content of a button laid out as a flex row unless told otherwise, and the line is a button so it can open. Chrome does not, which is why my preview rendered left-aligned and the app did not. The rule now says left explicitly, the page is rebuilt, and the app is relaunched with it. Open the arrow headband project and the lines sit on the left like every other row.

**Design artifacts, now updated.**

- Design System (version 32): a new `ChatTurnActivity` component with its guideline, a card showing Working, Done closed and Done open in light and dark, the coded React component in the bundle and typings, the two motion tokens, and a line in the brand book's Agent pane list. The ChatToolActivity guideline now says the card is only for a running action with measured progress.
- JusPrin v2 canvas (version 40): a "Chat/Turn Activity · Light & Dark" review board beside Chat/System Line on the component review page, the turn line drawn into the five print-timeline boards under the two person turns that made the Agent work, with the live app's own wording "Worked for 9s · 3 actions", and the proposal board redrawn with the chevron after the words.
